name: Chess
funFactCorrect: Modern chess arose in 1475, after an earlier version was changed to swap a weak minister piece for the queen, and an elephant piece for the bishop.
funFactIncorrect: Early versions of chess first appeared in India around the 6th century CE, thousands of years after the Old Kingdom period of ancient Egypt.

name: Dominoes
funFactCorrect: Most Western sets of dominoes come in a set of 28 pieces where dominoes range from 0-0 to 6-6, though some larger sets with more pieces run to 9-9 or 12-12.
funFactIncorrect: Dominoes originated in China in the 1300s, though they are quite different from Western dominoes like this, which were first recorded in 1700s Europe.

name: El Castillo
funFactCorrect: El Castillo was a Mayan temple, and was designed to create a moving shadow of the snake deity Kulkulkan on the Spring and Autumn equinoxes.
funFactIncorrect: While it might resemble Egyptian step pyramids, El Castillo was a Mayan temple built in the Chichen Itza complex.

name: 1800s British Coins
funFactCorrect: These coins were made during the reign of Queen Victoria, when the British still used a currency system of pounds, shillings, and pence.
funFactIncorrect: These coins were made in the United Kingdom during the reign of Queen Victoria, well after the end of Pharaonic Egypt.

name: Cave Canem Mosaic
funFactCorrect: The Cave Canem Mosaic is known as one of the earliest “beware of the dog” signs, and was one of many Pompeii mosaics that depicted a guard dog.
funFactIncorrect: The Cave Canem Mosaic is a Roman mosaic from the 1st century CE found at the House of the Tragic Poet in Pompeii.

name: Aztec Calendar Stone
funFactCorrect: The Aztec Calendar Stone, also known as the Sun Stone, was created in central Mexico thousands of years after Egypt's Old Kingdom.
funFactIncorrect: Although its circular design and detailed carvings might resemble an ancient Egyptian artefact, the Aztec Calendar Stone depicts Aztec religious and cosmological beliefs.

name: Haniwa Horse Figurine
funFactCorrect: Haniwa horse figurines were made from clay in ancient Japan during the Kofun period, somewhere between the third and sixth centuries CE.
funFactIncorrect: Although haniwa figurines were associated with burial practices, they were placed around Japanese burial mounds rather than inside Egyptian tombs.

name: Mayan Hieroglyphic Panel
funFactCorrect: The Maya civilisation developed its own hieroglyphic writing system in Mesoamerica, using symbols that represented words and sounds.
funFactIncorrect: Although Maya and Egyptian writing systems both used detailed symbols and images, these hieroglyphs belong to the Maya civilisation of South America.

name: Japanese Geta Sandals
funFactCorrect: Geta are traditional Japanese footwear made with raised wooden platforms, designed to help keep the wearer's feet above dirt, mud, and wet ground.
funFactIncorrect: Although ancient Egyptians also wore sandals, these traditional Japanese geta are distinguished by their wooden soles and raised supports.

name: Barrel of Monkeys
funFactCorrect: Barrel of Monkeys is a modern children's toy game in which players connect plastic monkeys by hooking their curved arms together to form a chain.
funFactIncorrect: These monkeys have curved arms designed to hook onto one another, allowing players to create a continuous chain by lifting one monkey at a time.
